findings.topic: Process model: the official app runs tailscaled IN-PROCESS as a gomobile library, not as a separate binary
findings.what: libtailscale is built with `gomobile bind` into an AAR (libgojni.so); Kotlin calls `Libtailscale.start(...)` once per app process and the Go side constructs tsd.System, wgengine, netstack and ipnlocal.LocalBackend inside the app process. The UI talks to LocalBackend by invoking the localapi http.Handler directly in memory (no unix socket, no `tailscale` CLI). There is no upstream mode in cmd/tailscaled that accepts a pre-opened TUN fd: `--tun=<name>` always goes through tstun.New -> tun.CreateTUN(name) (opens /dev/net/tun itself) or `userspace-networking`.

findings.implication_for_tailsocks: Keeping the daemon as a separate process means you cannot reuse libtailscale's Kotlin/Go glue as-is; you must add an fd-driven TUN path to cmd/tailscaled. The least invasive hook is a build-tagged android file in cmd/tailscaled that reassigns the package var `tstunNew` (tailscaled.go:793) to a function returning a device built from an inherited fd (see CreateUnmonitoredTUNFromFD finding) plus a router/DNS configurator equivalent to VPNFacade, keeping `--tun=<anything but userspace-networking>` so netns stays enabled (tailscaled.go:815). That is one new patch/file (netmon-style, like patch 06) rather than edits scattered across upstream. Root Mode (`--tun=tailscale0`) and Proxy Mode (`--tun=userspace-networking`) paths are untouched by such a hook.

findings.topic: How the VpnService fd reaches the Go engine (Builder -> establish -> detachFd -> CreateUnmonitoredTUNFromFD -> multiTUN)
findings.what: Go drives the Android Builder through gomobile interfaces: `IPNService.NewBuilder()` (Kotlin) returns a wrapper around `VpnService.Builder`; Go's `updateTUN` calls SetMTU/AddDNSServer/AddSearchDomain/AddRoute/ExcludeRoute/AddAddress, then `Establish()`; Kotlin wraps the returned `android.os.ParcelFileDescriptor`; Go calls `Detach()` == `ParcelFileDescriptor.detachFd()` to take raw ownership of the int fd, and creates a wireguard-go device with `tun.CreateUnmonitoredTUNFromFD(int(tunFD))`, which is then added to a `multiTUN` (a tun.Device that swaps underlying fds while wgengine sees one static device). CreateUnmonitoredTUNFromFD only does SetNonblock + os.NewFile + TUNGETIFF name lookup + initFromFlags; it does not set MTU and starts no netlink monitor. Builder details: allowFamily(AF_INET) and allowFamily(AF_INET6), setMetered(false) on Q+, setUnderlyingNetworks(cached NOT_VPN default network), setConfigureIntent, allowed/disallowed app lists; no setSession, no setBlocking, no allowBypass.

Close it instead"), :319-323 (`File()` panics: fd not constant on Android), :390-394 (`BatchSize() = 1`, Android disallows batching ioctls); wireguard-go tun_linux.go:631-688 (/home/pinus/go/pkg/mod/github.com/tailscale/wireguard-go@v0.0.0-20260715223240-2e01ba5b00f0/tun/tun_linux.go: SetNonblock, os.NewFile(fd,"/dev/tun"), Name() via TUNGETIFF at :320-340, initFromFlags, no setMTU/netlink).
findings.implication_for_tailsocks: With a separate daemon the fd must cross a process boundary. For the first TUN you can pass the detached fd via `exec.Cmd.ExtraFiles` (it becomes fd 3+ in the child), but because the official design re-establishes the VPN on every route/DNS change (see reconfiguration finding) you need a long-lived channel that can deliver a new fd at any time: a unix-domain socket with SCM_RIGHTS from the app to the daemon is the natural fit (the daemon already has a control socket dir, daemon.go:44). The daemon side should replicate multiTUN (a device wrapper that swaps the underlying fd, closes the old one, drops writes while 'down') so wgengine's single static `tun.Device` assumption holds. Use `tun.CreateUnmonitoredTUNFromFD` exactly as the official app does; TUNGETIFF/SIOCGIFMTU on the inherited fd work without root because the fd is a real tun fd created by the system for the VPN owner UID.

findings.topic: Engine wiring: wgengine + a real netstack are BOTH created; ProcessLocalIPs=false, ProcessSubnets=true, NetstackRouter=true
findings.what: The official backend creates the userspace engine with `Tun: multiTUN`, `Router: VPNFacade`, `DNS: VPNFacade`, `ReconfigureVPN: vf.ReconfigureVPN`, then still calls `netstack.Create(...)` and sets `ns.ProcessLocalIPs = false` ("let Android kernel handle it; VpnBuilder sets this up") and `ns.ProcessSubnets = true` ("for Android-being-an-exit-node support"), plus `sys.NetstackRouter.Set(true)`. Netstack remains essential in TUN mode: the tstun wrapper's outbound intercept hands host packets destined to 100.100.100.100 / fd7a:115c:a1e0::53 to netstack, which terminates MagicDNS (UDP 53), DNS/HTTP over TCP 53/80/8080 (web client, Taildrive) locally and never forwards quad-100 to a peer. ProcessSubnets=true lets netstack forward inbound peer traffic to non-local IPs (this node acting as exit node/subnet router) because there is no kernel forwarding on Android. On mobile the router is wrapped in `router.ConsolidatingRoutes` to keep the route count small (Android TransactionTooLargeException around ~4000 routes).

In cmd/tailscaled that is the non-onlyNetstack branch of tryEngine (tailscaled.go:833-876) plus `handleSubnetsInNetstack()` which returns false on android (tailscaled.go:777-791) — you would need to force `netstackSubnetRouter = true` (e.g. env `TS_DEBUG_NETSTACK_SUBNETS=1`, tailscaled.go:778, no patch needed) if you want the phone to serve as exit node/subnet router. Patches 08 (UseNetstackForIP for the service IP), 09 (fake-TUN loopback injection) and 14 (forwarder via netstack) exist only because there is no real TUN; they remain needed for Proxy mode but are bypassed in fd-TUN mode, so no new netstack patches are required for MagicDNS at 100.100.100.100 — it works via handleLocalPackets as in the official app.

findings.topic: DNS: 100.100.100.100 (+ fd7a:115c:a1e0::53) is always the VPN's DNS server; OS base resolvers come from Kotlin LinkProperties and feed the in-daemon forwarder
findings.what: VPNFacade reports `SupportsSplitDNS() == false`, so dns.Manager.compileConfig always ends in the 'OS cannot split-DNS' branch: `ocfg.Nameservers = cfg.serviceIPs()` (100.100.100.100 and fd7a:115c:a1e0::53) whenever the netmap has any DNS routes or default resolvers, `rcfg.Routes["."]` is set to the base (OS) nameservers obtained via `OSConfigurator.GetBaseConfig()`, and base search domains are appended to tailnet search domains. `MatchDomains` is computed but ignored by updateTUN. GetBaseConfig on Android parses a two-line string ("servers\nsearch domains") that Kotlin maintains from `LinkProperties.dnsServers`/`domains` of the best NOT_VPN network; if no servers are found it falls back to Google DNS when BuildConfig.USE_GOOGLE_DNS_FALLBACK is set. updateTUN then calls `addDnsServer` for each ocfg.Nameserver and `addSearchDomain(dom.WithoutTrailingDot())` for each search domain; ChromeOS gets Google DNS if the list is empty because ChromeOS erases platform DNS otherwise. routerConfigLocked adds /32 and /128 routes for the service IPs so the DNS IP is routed into the TUN. Note the trivial 'override DNS with plain IPs' case sets ocfg.Nameservers to the admin's resolvers directly (not quad-100).

findings.implication_for_tailsocks: TUN mode can drop the hev `mapdns` hack and the app-side DNS proxy (appctr/dns.go, TunVpnService.kt:32-33,43) entirely: the VpnService gets `addDnsServer(100.100.100.100)` plus tailnet+OS search domains, and the daemon's own forwarder answers/forwards. What TailSocks must supply is a `dns.OSConfigurator` inside the daemon whose GetBaseConfig returns the phone's real resolvers (LinkProperties.dnsServers) and whose SetDNS hands the OSConfig to the app for the Builder. Patch 11 (TS_DNS_FALLBACK in noopManager) is the static ancestor of this; the official design updates it live on every network change (onDNSConfigChanged -> NetworkChanged -> netmon.InjectEvent -> wgengine relink -> dns.Set + ReconfigureVPN). Because Android VpnService has no split-DNS API, all DNS goes through quad-100 — this is exactly what makes MagicDNS and split DNS work 'natively'. Keep MatchDomains out of the Builder as upstream does.

findings.topic: Routes: rcfg.Routes -> addRoute; LocalRoutes -> excludeRoute (API 33+) or subtracted CIDR set (older); exit node adds 0.0.0.0/0 and ::/0; LAN access via LocalRoutes
findings.what: router.Config.Routes (peer /32,/128, accepted subnet routes, exit-node default routes, service IPs) are added with `addRoute(prefix.Masked())`. For exit nodes LocalBackend guarantees both AllIPv4 and AllIPv6 are present (blackhole fill) and computes `internalAndExternalInterfaces()` from netmon's interface list: internal (loopback/link-local/VM) prefixes always go to LocalRoutes; external LAN prefixes go to LocalRoutes only if ExitNodeAllowLANAccess, otherwise they are appended to Routes so LAN traffic is deliberately pulled into the tunnel (no leak). This switch explicitly includes GOOS=android. On API >= 33 the official app calls `Builder.excludeRoute(IpPrefix)` for each LocalRoute (skipping loopback, which VpnService rejects); on older APIs it computes Routes minus LocalRoutes as a minimal CIDR list (`ranges_calc.Calculate`) and addRoute's the result. Interface data on Android comes from Kotlin `NetworkInterface.getNetworkInterfaces()` serialized to JSON and registered via `netmon.RegisterInterfaceGetter`.

With minSdk 24 you need the pre-33 path (port ranges_calc.go, BSD-3-Clause) and the 33+ excludeRoute path. Stop hardcoding 100.64.0.0/10 and fd7a:115c:a1e0::/48 (TunVpnService.kt:222-226) — use rcfg.Routes so subnet routes, exit nodes and the service IPs come for free, and honour LocalRoutes for 'Allow LAN access'. findings.topic: Loop prevention: per-socket VpnService.protect() + Network.bindSocket via netns hooks, set only after the VpnService exists; then a magicsock rebind
findings.what: The Go engine never marks sockets itself on Android (`netns.UseSocketMark()` is false). Instead netns_android.go's `controlC` — the Dialer/ListenConfig Control hook used by magicsock UDP sockets, DERP HTTP client, tsdial system dials, logtail, etc. — calls two process-global funcs: `androidProtectFunc(fd)` and `androidBindToNetworkFunc(fd)`. The official app registers them when Kotlin calls `Libtailscale.requestVPN(service)`: protect maps to the inherited `VpnService.protect(int)`, bind maps to `Network.bindSocket(fd)` on the cached NOT_VPN default network. Because sockets opened before the service existed are unprotected, it immediately calls `b.backend.DebugRebind()` to recreate magicsock sockets. On disconnect both funcs are reset to nil. The app's own package is NOT excluded from the VPN (in allow-list mode it is even added to the allowed set) — the app relies entirely on protect(). The comment notes VpnService.protect is an IPC to another process that sets the fwmark. Crucially, `netns.SetEnabled(!onlyNetstack)` means in `--tun=userspace-networking` mode the Control hook is disabled and these funcs would never run.

findings.implication_for_tailsocks: Two viable designs for a separate-process daemon. (A) UID-wide exclusion (what TunVpnService.kt:229-247 already does with addDisallowedApplication for io.github.bropines.tailscaled*): Android VPN app rules are per UID, so every socket of the child tailscaled bypasses the TUN with zero IPC — simplest and robust, but the app's own process is also outside the VPN (its UI/Taildrive WebDAV client/CLI cannot reach tailnet IPs through the TUN; the official app avoids that by dialing in-process via netstack), and behaviour under Always-on lockdown needs testing. (B) Faithful port: keep the daemon inside the VPN and protect each socket: run the daemon with netns enabled (not userspace-networking), and give it protect/bind implementations — e.g. the daemon sends the fd over a unix socket (SCM_RIGHTS) to the app, which calls VpnService.protect(fd) and Network.bindSocket(fd) and replies; since the fwmark sticks to the socket, protection survives the round trip. Talking to /dev/socket/fwmarkd directly from Go is possible in principle but undocumented. Either way replicate the `DebugRebind()` after protect becomes available, and clear the hooks on disconnect.

findings.topic: Reconfiguration lifecycle: Router.Set/SetDNS are buffered in VPNFacade; wgengine's ReconfigureVPN hook triggers a full new Builder + establish whenever routes or DNS differ; multiTUN swaps fds
findings.what: VPNFacade implements both router.Router and dns.OSConfigurator but only stores the configs. wgengine calls `ReconfigureVPN()` (a) at the end of Reconfig after `e.dns.Set` succeeds when router or DNS changed, and (b) after a major link change on android/linux/ios/darwin/openbsd. `ReconfigureVPN` calls `SetBoth(rcfg, dcfg)`, which pushes the pair into runBackend's `configs` channel and blocks on `configErrs` until updateTUN returns — i.e. the Builder work is synchronous with wgengine.Reconfig. runBackend only calls `updateTUN` when `vpnService.service != nil` and `isConfigNonNilAndDifferent` (reflect.DeepEqual against last applied rcfg/dcfg) — so every netmap change that alters routes/DNS produces a brand-new `establish()` and the new fd replaces the old in multiTUN (old device closed; comment says pending Reads are never unblocked by Android so they close it 'and hope that no packets are lost'). If `len(rcfg.LocalAddrs)==0` (stopped) it closes all TUNs and brings multiTUN Down so writes are dropped instead of deadlocking. State-driven path: when ipn.State >= Starting and a VpnService exists, updateTUN also runs. Teardown: `ServiceDisconnect` -> Down + CloseTUNs + clear protect funcs; `closeVpnService` on Builder errors sets WantRunning=false and stops the service; `onRevoke` (another VPN took over) sets WantRunning=false, marks VPN unprepared, closes. A new IPNService instance is detected by a random per-instance ID.

findings.implication_for_tailsocks: The daemon must be the source of truth for Builder parameters and must be able to request a re-establish at any time; the app must reply with a fresh fd. Design the daemon->app RPC as 'apply VPN config {addrs, routes, localRoutes, dns, searchDomains, mtu}' returning {fd or error}, invoked from a VPNFacade-equivalent's ReconfigureVPN, and keep it synchronous so wgengine.Reconfig sees Builder errors (INTERACT_ACROSS_USERS, revoked permission -> null from establish). Implement the DeepEqual gate to avoid needless re-establish (each establish briefly interrupts traffic). Handle the reverse direction too: onRevoke/stop in the app must tell the daemon to Down/close the TUN device and, if using design B, clear protect hooks. Today TunVpnService restarts only when the exit-node id changes (TunVpnService.kt:160-171); the official model replaces that heuristic with config equality.

findings.topic: MTU, IPv6 and TUN I/O characteristics
findings.what: The official app hardcodes `defaultMTU = 1280` (wgengine's minimal/safe MTU) and calls `Builder.setMtu(1280)`; multiTUN.MTU() returns the underlying device's MTU (read via SIOCGIFMTU on the tun name) or 1280 when no device is attached. IPv6 is fully enabled: allowFamily(AF_INET6), the node's /128 ULA is added with addAddress, IPv6 routes/::/0 are added, and the IPv6 service IP fd7a:115c:a1e0::53 is offered as a DNS server. multiTUN.BatchSize() returns 1 because Android disallows the ioctls needed for TUN batching/offload; the fd is created 'unmonitored' (no netlink link-state listener).
findings.evidence: libtailscale/tailscale.go:27 (`const defaultMTU = 1280 // minimalMTU from wgengine/userspace.go`); net.go:107-110 (`builder.SetMTU(defaultMTU)`); multitun.go:173-179 (MTU reply defaults to defaultMTU), :390-394 (`BatchSize() int { return 1 }` with comment); IPNService.kt:193-194 (`allowFamily(OsConstants.AF_INET)`, `allowFamily(OsConstants.AF_INET6)`); net.go:193-197 (addAddress for every LocalAddrs prefix incl. /128); upstream net/tstun/mtu.go:77-79 (`safeTUNMTU TUNMTU = 1280`), :133-148 (`DefaultTUNMTU`); wireguard-go tun_linux.go:285-310 (MTU via SIOCGIFMTU), :631-688 (CreateUnmonitoredTUNFromFD).
findings.implication_for_tailsocks: Set MTU 1280 on the Builder (TunVpnService currently uses TUN_MTU; keep 1280 unless you have measurements), always allowFamily both and add both node addresses — IPv6 should not be an opt-in toggle in the official design because DNS over fd7a:115c:a1e0::53 and IPv6 peers depend on it (TunVpnService.kt:199-226 makes v6 optional today). Expect single-packet TUN reads/writes (no GRO/GSO); the double-stack overhead of hev goes away, which is the main performance win of the rebuild.

findings.topic: Always-on VPN and lockdown handling in the official app
findings.what: The manifest declares IPNService with `android.permission.BIND_VPN_SERVICE`, the `android.net.VpnService` intent-filter and `foregroundServiceType="systemExempted"`; it does not opt out of always-on (no SUPPORTS_ALWAYS_ON=false meta-data), so the system may start the service itself. onStartCommand treats the system's `"android.net.VpnService"` action as an Always-on start: posts a non-foreground notification (because the system did not start it as foreground), sets WantRunning=true and calls `Libtailscale.requestVPN(this)`; a restart with a null intent (after OOM kill) re-requests the VPN if the backend was previously able to run. There is no explicit lockdown (`isLockdownEnabled`) handling anywhere; loop avoidance under lockdown relies on protect(). User-initiated starts go through `VpnService.prepare()` (AppViewModel/VpnViewModel, StartVPNWorker for broadcast intents, QuickToggleService), with a conflict dialog when another VPN is active; `onRevoke` flips the prepared flag so prepare() is shown again. findings.topic: How the official Android app owns the TUN (the model to copy)
findings.what: The official libtailscale never uses tstun.New or --tun. It builds wgengine.Config with Tun = a multiTUN (a tun.Device that can swap the underlying NativeTun), Router = DNS = a VPNFacade that just records router.Config/dns.OSConfig, and ReconfigureVPN = facade.ReconfigureVPN which delivers both configs to updateTUN. updateTUN builds a fresh VpnService.Builder every time routes/DNS change (setMtu 1280, addDnsServer for dcfg.Nameservers, addSearchDomain, addRoute for rcfg.Routes, excludeRoute for rcfg.LocalRoutes on API 33+ or range subtraction below, addAddress for LocalAddrs), calls establish(), detachFd(), tun.CreateUnmonitoredTUNFromFD, and adds the new device to multiTUN; the old fd is closed because pending reads never unblock. Netstack is created with ProcessLocalIPs=false, ProcessSubnets=true, NetstackRouter=true. The app's own package is NOT excluded from the VPN (only user/MDM-selected packages are), and underlay sockets are protected through netns.SetAndroidProtectFunc -> VpnService.protect plus SetAndroidBindToNetworkFunc; because sockets bound before the VPN existed are unprotected, it calls DebugRebind() right after the service appears. Network changes are pushed from Kotlin via NetworkChanged(ifname) -> netmon.UpdateLastKnownDefaultRouteInterface + netMon.InjectEvent(). Upstream DNS servers are read from Android LinkProperties and returned through GetBaseConfigFunc (falling back to Google DNS).

findings.topic: Routes/DNS cannot be static: Android requires re-establish, so the fd must be swappable at runtime (ExtraFiles alone is insufficient)
findings.what: Android has no API to change routes/DNS of an established VPN; the official app re-runs Builder.establish() on every rcfg/dcfg change (exit node on/off adds 0.0.0.0/0 + ::/0 and LocalRoutes, subnet routes come and go with the netmap, MagicDNS/search domains change) and swaps the NativeTun under wireguard-go via multiTUN, closing the old fd. The daemon only learns the final route set after it has connected to control (routerConfigLocked runs from authReconfig), so at spawn time there is nothing to establish yet; the official multiTUN blocks Read until a device is added and uses Down() to make Write return while no device exists.

findings.topic: Underlay option 1: run the daemon under the app uid and exclude the app (addDisallowedApplication)
findings.what: The daemon is a child process of the app (exec), hence same uid; Android VPN routing is uid-based, so addDisallowedApplication(own package) keeps every socket of the daemon out of the TUN with no daemon change at all: on android netns.control returns controlC, which does nothing unless SetAndroidProtectFunc/SetAndroidBindToNetworkFunc were registered (they are not in the daemon), and netns is enabled in TUN mode. The cost: the daemon's OS-level dials to tailnet IPs also bypass the TUN. In kernel-TUN mode tsdial.dialOneUser goes UseNetstackForIP (nil unless onlyNetstack) -> d.routes (nil on Android: ShouldUseRoutes requires the user-dial-routes control knob, so wgengine calls SetRoutes(nil,nil)) -> plain net.Dialer, i.e. a kernel socket that, with the uid excluded, exits via Wi-Fi/cellular and never reaches a peer. This breaks the SOCKS5/HTTP proxy (Dialer: dialer.UserDial), peerapi/Taildrop sends (dialPeerAPI -> getPeerDialer), Taildrive dials (patch 10 uses UserDial) and DNS forwarding to tailnet resolvers. Fix within upstream mechanisms: also set dialer.UseNetstackForIP + NetstackDialTCP/UDP in fd mode (drop the onlyNetstack gating at two sites) and set ns.CheckLocalTransportEndpoints = true, which is the documented tsnet mechanism for 'outbound connections when ProcessLocalIPs is false (i.e., when using a TUN)': shouldProcessInbound then FindTransportEndpoint()s replies to netstack-originated flows; netstack's outbound path already sends non-service-IP packets to WireGuard via InjectOutboundPacketBuffer, and patched DialContextTCP/UDP bind the source to the node's own IP so replies match. PeerForIP returns the exit node for non-tailnet IPs when an exit node is set, preserving today's proxy-mode semantics.

findings.topic: Underlay option 2: VpnService.protect over a Unix-socket callback (app uid inside the VPN, the official model)
findings.what: netns_android.go already provides the hooks: SetAndroidProtectFunc(f) and SetAndroidBindToNetworkFunc(f) are called from controlC for every socket created through netns, which is the single choke point for all underlay sockets: magicsock UDP listeners and pings, DERP HTTP/TLS dials, control/SystemDial, dnsfallback, netcheck STUN sockets and portmapper. In a separate process the daemon can implement f(fd) as: send fd over the control socket with SCM_RIGHTS, the app's Go bridge receives it and calls a Kotlin callback that invokes VpnService.protect(fd) on the running service, then acks. Protection is a property of the underlying socket (netd sets the fwmark on the socket, not on the fd number), so protecting the received duplicate protects the daemon's socket. Caveats mirrored from the official app: sockets created before the VPN exists are unprotected, so after establish the app should trigger magicsock Rebind via LocalAPI (/localapi/v0/debug?action=rebind -> DebugRebind -> MagicConn().Rebind()); SystemDial connections are tracked in activeSysConns and closed on link change so control/DERP re-dial protected. With the app uid inside the VPN, UserDial's plain kernel dial (tsdial.go:610-611) routes into the TUN and back into tailscaled, so SOCKS5/HTTP proxy, peerapi, Taildrive and DNS forwarding to tailnet resolvers work with no netstack/tsdial changes and exit-node semantics (0/0 route) apply to SOCKS clients too; patch 14 becomes unnecessary in fd mode (still needed for proxy mode).

open_questions: Does VpnService.protect(fd) applied in the app process to an SCM_RIGHTS-received duplicate reliably protect the daemon's socket on all target ROMs (netd marks the socket object, so it should, but this is Android-internals behaviour not verifiable from the repos; must be tested on the author's device, including Android 7-9).

Is the app itself acceptable inside the VPN (option 2)? Today all io.github.bropines.tailscaled* packages are excluded (TunVpnService.kt:230-247); putting the app inside changes where the app's own non-SOCKS traffic (WebUI clients, control-proxy resolution in daemon.go:195-231, ByeDPI) goes, especially with an exit node.

Does netmon_linux's AF_NETLINK RTMGRP bind (patch 13 makes it build on android) succeed for an unprivileged app on Android 11+, or does the daemon silently run on polling? Related: after the rebuild, should the control channel also carry netchange -> netMon.InjectEvent() to replace the spawn-time TS_NET_STATE snapshot (patch 06)?

Do the SELinux rules on all supported Android versions (7+) permit TUNGETIFF ioctl on the VpnService fd from an app process that is not the one that called establish()? The official app does it in the same process; here the fd crosses to a child process of the same uid/domain, so the same policy should apply, but it is untested.

Startup ordering: the daemon has no TUN until the first ReconfigureVPN after connecting to control. Should the app pre-establish a minimal TUN (CGNAT + service IP routes) and pass it via ExtraFiles for faster first packets, or accept the official app's lazy behaviour? Also, how should the daemon behave when the app never answers (VPN permission revoked / onRevoke) — Down() the fdTUN and keep running, or exit?

findings.topic: How the official client does it (reference model to copy)
findings.what: libtailscale wires wgengine with Tun = multiTUN (a tun.Device that accepts fds at runtime), Router = DNS = VPNFacade (a copy of router.CallbackRouter; SetBoth is called on ReconfigureVPN), then on every config change updateTUN builds a fresh VpnService.Builder: setMtu(1280), addDnsServer for each dcfg.Nameservers, addSearchDomain, rcfg.Routes -> addRoute, rcfg.LocalRoutes -> excludeRoute (API>=33) or rangescalc.Calculate(Routes,LocalRoutes) -> addRoute on older APIs, rcfg.LocalAddrs -> addAddress, establish, detachFd, tun.CreateUnmonitoredTUNFromFD, multiTUN.add (old device closed). findings.topic: Where tailscaled must be patched for an fd-based Android TUN

findings.topic: Why uid exclusion forces a 'hybrid' netstack dialer in TUN mode (SOCKS/HTTP proxies, patch 14, Taildrive)
findings.what: The SOCKS5 and HTTP proxies dial with tsdial.Dialer.UserDial. dialOneUser uses netstack only if UseNetstackForIP says so; otherwise it uses the 'peer dialer' (a plain net.Dialer on Android, because net/tsdial has no peerdial_*.go and peerDialControlFunc stays nil) or SystemDial, i.e. an OS socket. With the app's UID disallowed from the VPN those sockets never enter the TUN, so proxies, patch 14's split-DNS-to-peer path (viaNetstack also keys off UseNetstackForIP) and any in-daemon peer dial would break. Netstack replies for netstack-originated flows arrive with dst = local IP; with ProcessLocalIPs=false they are only handled if CheckLocalTransportEndpoints is true (tsnet sets it for exactly this TUN case). --socks5-server / --outbound-http-proxy-listen are not tied to userspace-networking and start regardless.
findings.evidence: cmd/tailscaled/proxy.go:34-35, :88-103 (UserDial); net/tsdial/tsdial.go:587-604 (dialOneUser), :347-363 (peerDialControlFunc nil), directory listing net/tsdial (no peerdial file); wgengine/netstack/netstack.go:187-196 (CheckLocalTransportEndpoints doc), :1339-1345 (inbound decision); tsnet/tsnet.go:883 (precedent); net/dns/resolver/forwarder.go:858-866 (viaNetstack); tailscaled.go:689-691 (proxy started irrespective of onlyNetstack); tailscaled.go:718-726 (UseNetstackForIP pattern to reuse).

With that, SOCKS5/HTTP on loopback/LAN keep working while TUN is active (still useful for LAN-access clients and excluded apps), Taildrive's SOCKS-based proxy (drive.go) is untouched, and patch 14 stays effective. Answer to 'proxies while TUN active': keep offering them; document them as redundant for on-device apps.

findings.topic: DNS in native TUN mode: what the Builder gets and what quad-100 forwards to

findings.topic: Route computation and the semantics of 'full tunnel', 'split', 'LAN access'
findings.what: router.Config is produced by ipnlocal.routerConfigLocked: LocalAddrs = node addresses; Routes = route manager's OS routes (peers, accepted subnet routes when RouteAll/accept_routes); when an exit node is set, 0.0.0.0/0 and ::/0 are appended if missing, and LAN handling uses interface discovery: LocalRoutes = internal IPs (+ external LAN IPs if ExitNodeAllowLANAccess) else LAN prefixes are explicitly routed INTO the tunnel to avoid leaks; quad-100 /32 and /128 and hosted VIP-service IPs are added. On Android the OS gets 100.64.0.0/10 as one route only when no other interface has a CGNAT address (shouldUseOneCGNATRoute), and re-establishing the VpnService on route changes is documented as tearing down long-lived TCP connections.

findings.topic: Route-churn trap: tun0 is not recognised as the Tailscale interface
findings.what: netmon.isTailscaleInterface only recognises the interface name registered via SetTailscaleInterfaceProps or names starting with 'tailscale'; tailscaled only calls SetTailscaleInterfaceProps on plan9. An Android VpnService interface is 'tun0' with the node's 100.x address, so once it is up Monitor.HasCGNATInterface() returns true, shouldUseOneCGNATRoute returns false, and routes become per-peer /32s that change on every peer join/leave — each change re-establishes the VPN interface. (netmon.LocalAddresses does skip Tailscale IPs, so magicsock endpoints are fine.)

findings.what: On Android the daemon's netmon default route is whatever the app last told it (defaultRoute() returns lastKnownDefaultRouteIfName; likelyHomeRouterIP uses the pushed gateway), polling is every 10 minutes on android, and the official app pushes iface/gateway/DNS from a ConnectivityManager callback filtered on NET_CAPABILITY_NOT_VPN and calls netMon.InjectEvent() plus setUnderlyingNetworks(). TailSocks uses registerDefaultNetworkCallback, which after the VPN is up reports the VPN network itself, and only feeds the bridge (not the child).

findings.topic: Loop prevention without VpnService.protect()
findings.what: protect() is a VpnService instance method; the child process cannot call it (it would need per-socket fd passing to the app). netns_android's controlC is a no-op when no protect/bind funcs are registered, so netns being enabled in TUN mode (netns.SetEnabled(!onlyNetstack)) is harmless. TailSocks already relies on Builder.addDisallowedApplication for every io.github.bropines.tailscaled* package (needs QUERY_ALL_PACKAGES, present in the manifest); since the child runs under the same UID, all of its sockets (WireGuard UDP, DERP, control, DoH) bypass the VPN by uid routing rule.
findings.evidence: net/netns/netns_android.go:50-108 (hooks nil => no-op); tailscaled.go:815 (netns.SetEnabled); TunVpnService.kt:230-247 (self-exclusion); AndroidManifest.xml (QUERY_ALL_PACKAGES uses-permission); tailscale-android/libtailscale/backend.go:215-244 (official protect/bind + DebugRebind workaround).
findings.implication_for_tailsocks: Keep uid self-exclusion as THE loop guard (add the .dev suffix package as today). Consequences to accept: the app's own process never routes through the tunnel (same as now; Taildrive/WebUI go via SOCKS/LocalAPI), and nothing in the daemon may rely on OS sockets reaching tailnet IPs (hence the hybrid netstack dialer). Do not mix addAllowedApplication with disallowed lists (Android forbids both).

findings.topic: fd hand-off design: why a runtime SCM_RIGHTS channel is required (not just ExtraFiles)
findings.what: Builder.addAddress must be the node's real Tailscale IP (peers reject other sources under WireGuard AllowedIPs), which is only known after the daemon has a netmap, and routes/DNS change over time (exit node on/off, subnet routes, VIP services). The official app therefore establishes a NEW interface on each config change and feeds fds to a multiTUN. Inheriting one fd at exec (cmd.ExtraFiles -> fd 3 -> TS_TUN_FD) can only serve a static first config and cannot re-establish. Android LocalSocket supports setFileDescriptorsForSend; Go can do syscall.UnixRights/unix.Sendmsg on both ends.
findings.evidence: tailscale-android/libtailscale/net.go:193-247 (address from rcfg.LocalAddrs, establish/detach per config), multitun.go:153-172 (device replacement); tailscale_src/ipn/ipnlocal/local.go:6525-6531 (LocalAddrs from cfg.Addresses); wireguard-go tun/tun_linux.go:660-690 (CreateUnmonitoredTUNFromFD takes an int fd).
findings.implication_for_tailsocks: Protocol on a UNIX socket the bridge listens on (path in env TS_ANDROID_VPN_SOCK, connected by the child at startup): daemon->bridge newline-JSON {config: addrs, routes, localRoutes, dns, searchDomains, mtu} from CallbackRouter.SetBoth (nil/empty LocalAddrs => {down}); bridge->Kotlin via a gomobile interface (like the existing CloseCallBack Closer, appctr.go:120) returning a detached fd int; bridge->daemon {tun} with the fd as SCM_RIGHTS ancillary data; Kotlin->bridge->daemon {down} on revoke/stop; bridge->daemon {netstate} for network changes; daemon->bridge {status: established/failed} to update the notification/UI. Keep the last config in the bridge so excluded-apps edits can re-establish without a daemon round trip.

findings.topic: Failure mode: VPN permission revoked or another VPN takes the slot
findings.what: Today onRevoke stops hev and the VpnService. In the new model only the daemon can close its fd, so revoke must be relayed. The official client reacts by turning Tailscale off (setWantRunning(false), prepared=false). TailSocks can instead keep the daemon running: with the hybrid dialer the SOCKS5/HTTP proxies and the bridge DNS proxy keep working, only OS-level routing is lost.
findings.evidence: TunVpnService.kt:135-144 (onRevoke today); tailscale-android/android/.../IPNService.kt:123-131; libtailscale/backend.go:253-262 (onDisconnect => devices.Down + CloseTUNs); multitun.go:295-317 (Down drops writes without blocking).
findings.implication_for_tailsocks: onRevoke -> bridge.tunDown() -> daemon multiTUN.Down()+Shutdown(); mark 'VPN needs permission' (do not silently flip tun_mode_enabled off as TunPermissionActivity does on denial), show a notification 'running in proxy-only mode, tap to re-enable', and on the next START/APPLY run TunPermissionActivity again and then ask the daemon to ReconfigureVPN. The daemon must treat a dead fd (EOF/EBADF from the kernel when the slot is taken) the same way: close it and continue with writes dropped.

findings.topic: Failure mode: establish() returns null / INTERACT_ACROSS_USERS / not prepared
findings.what: Builder.establish() returns null when the app is not prepared or was revoked, and throws with INTERACT_ACROSS_USERS on multi-user devices. Upstream records a router.Set error in health and still proceeds to DNS config; the official app closes the VPN service and sets WantRunning=false on error.

findings.implication_for_tailsocks: Return the failure from SetBoth so it surfaces as router health (visible in status/notification), keep the daemon alive, and retry via ReconfigureVPN once TunPermissionActivity reports RESULT_OK. Treat an establish() exception as 'TUN unavailable, proxy-only' rather than stopping the node.

findings.topic: Failure mode: daemon crash while the VPN is up, or the app dying while the daemon lives
findings.what: If the child dies, its TUN fd closes and the kernel removes tun0; the supervisor goroutine calls Stop() and CloseCallBack.Close() => stopMe(), which today also stops hev; auto-reconnect restarts the daemon after 3 unhealthy ticks. If instead the APP process is killed, the child keeps running (killall only at next start) and, in TUN mode, keeps the VPN fd — a VPN with no VpnService behind it.
findings.evidence: appctr/appctr.go:559-585 (supervisor), :735-743 (Stop signals the child), :800-802 (killall leftovers on next start); TailscaledService.kt:815 (closeCallBack = stopMe), :881-928 (stopMe), :255-321 (auto-reconnect); tailscaled.go:272-274, :928-932 (TS_PARENT_DEATH_FD).
findings.implication_for_tailsocks: On child death: TunVpnService.stopSelf() + clear notification (fd is gone anyway); auto-reconnect brings a new daemon up which re-requests a config and re-establishes with no dialog (prepare() stays granted). On app death: pass a pipe in cmd.ExtraFiles and set TS_PARENT_DEATH_FD so the daemon exits with the app (also good for proxy mode). Verify on-device what Android does with an established VPN whose VpnService process died but whose fd is still open (see open questions).

Go ApplySettings already restarts on 'critical' option changes; Tasker, AppFunctions, widgets and the settings toggle only flip tun_mode_enabled and send ACTION_APPLY_SETTINGS; the status broadcast's tun_enabled extra reports the preference, not whether a VPN is actually established.

design.summary:
Design for TailSocks TUN mode "the official way" with the daemon kept as a separate process: the Kotlin VpnService still creates the TUN, but the fd is handed to the spawned tailscaled over an inherited AF_UNIX socketpair with SCM_RIGHTS, and tailscaled itself drives wireguard-go on it through a swappable multiTUN device. The daemon becomes the single source of truth for VPN configuration exactly as in tailscale-android: an android-only file in cmd/tailscaled installs router.CallbackRouter as both Router and dns.OSConfigurator, wgengine's ReconfigureVPN hook flushes {LocalAddrs, Routes, LocalRoutes, Nameservers, SearchDomains} to the app, the app runs VpnService.Builder + establish() + detachFd() and returns a fresh fd; every netmap/DNS/link change that alters the config re-establishes (Android has no incremental API), and the old fd is closed. hev-socks5-tunnel, the hev YAML/JNI layer, the fake 10.0.0.1/8 gateway, hard-coded 100.64.0.0/10 routes and the exit-node-id restart heuristic all go away; MagicDNS, split DNS, search domains, subnet routes, exit nodes (with the upstream ExitNodeAllowLANAccess semantics) and the 100.100.100.100 service IP work natively because netstack keeps terminating quad-100 with a real TUN (ProcessLocalIPs=false, ProcessSubnets=true, NetstackRouter=true, like libtailscale/backend.go:352-359).

Loop prevention stays UID-based (addDisallowedApplication for the app's own packages, TunVpnService.kt:230-247): the child shares the UID, so all of its control/DERP/WireGuard/DNS-forwarder sockets bypass the VPN with zero IPC, and no DebugRebind hack is needed. The price is that the daemon's OS-level UserDial cannot reach the tailnet through the TUN, so fd mode also enables the "hybrid" netstack dialer (UseNetstackForIP + NetstackDialTCP/UDP + CheckLocalTransportEndpoints), which keeps the SOCKS5/HTTP proxies, Taildrop peerapi, Taildrive and patch 14's split-DNS-via-peer path working while the TUN is up.

Daemon footprint: one new android-only file pair (android_vpn.go + a vendored copy of multitun.go), ~12 inserted lines in cmd/tailscaled/tailscaled.go, 3 changed lines in cmd/tailscaled/netstack.go, and a small upgrade to the existing fix_android_netmon.go (live interface snapshot with real prefix lengths). Folded into the existing patches 06 and 08 the count stays at 15 (the tree already has 15, not 13). Proxy mode (--tun=userspace-networking) and Root Mode (--tun=tailscale0 via su, osrouter from patch 13) never enter the new branch and keep the same arguments and binaries. The plan is six steps; after every step the app builds and ships (steps 1-2 are dark, step 3 is opt-in behind a hidden engine flag, step 4 flips the default, step 5 deletes hev).

== 5. How the daemon's own traffic avoids the VPN ==
UID exclusion. Android VPN routing is per UID; the daemon is exec'd by the app (daemon.go:51) so it shares the UID and every socket it opens (magicsock UDP, DERP/TLS, control HTTPS, netcheck STUN, DNS forwarder upstream sockets incl. DoH, logtail) leaves through the underlying network without any per-socket work. netns.SetEnabled(true) in fd mode is harmless (netns_android.go:26-28 UseSocketMark=false; :72-108 controlC no-op with nil funcs). Under Always-on lockdown the VPN's own package is exempted from the "require VPN" uid ranges by the platform, so this should keep working (device check listed). Consequence handled by the hybrid dialer (2a/2b): tsdial.dialOneUser (tsdial.go:587-611) would otherwise fall to a plain net.Dialer for tailnet IPs, and with the UID excluded that socket exits via Wi-Fi/LTE and never reaches a peer; with UseNetstackForIP + NetstackDial* set, SOCKS5/HTTP (cmd/tailscaled/proxy.go UserDial), Taildrop's peerapi dials, Taildrive (patch 10) and patch 14's viaNetstack() (forwarder.go:853-866) all go netstack -> WireGuard, and CheckLocalTransportEndpoints delivers their replies (dst = own IP) back into gVisor instead of the kernel (netstack.go:1339-1345). PeerForIP returns the exit node for foreign IPs when one is set, so SOCKS semantics with an exit node are unchanged from today.

== 6. DNS, routes, exit node on netmap changes ==
DNS: dns.Manager.compileConfig with a non-split OSConfigurator ends in ocfg.Nameservers = serviceIPs (manager.go:376-398). TailSocks always pushes OverrideDNSResolvers (appctr.go:386-412) with the DoH URL first; a DoH resolver makes hasDefaultIPResolversOnly() false (net/dns/config.go:123-133), so the "trivial: hand IPs to the OS" case (manager.go:337-351) is skipped and rcfg.Routes["."] = DefaultResolvers with quad-100 on the Builder (manager.go:352-356). If a user removes DoH and MagicDNS/split routes are absent, the OS gets the plain IPs directly, which is the correct upstream semantics. Packets from the TUN to 100.100.100.100/fd7a:115c:a1e0::53 are absorbed by netstack.handleLocalPackets (netstack.go:842-872), answered by MagicDNS/split routes/forwarder, injected back. ipnlocal adds 100.100.100.100/32 and the v6 /128 to Routes (local.go:6593-6599) so the DNS IP is routed into the TUN. Base (carrier/Wi-Fi) resolvers reach the forwarder via GetBaseConfigFunc from netstate frames, with TS_DNS_FALLBACK as fallback; RecompileDNSConfig re-runs compileConfig on change. The hev mapdns hack and the on-device use of the bridge's UDP DNS proxy (appctr/dns.go:25) are no longer needed; the proxy stays listening for LAN clients only.
Routes: rcfg.Routes = peers (one 100.64.0.0/10 once tun0 is registered, see 2c), accepted subnet routes (RouteAll = accept_routes, appctr.go:374-375), exit node 0.0.0.0/0 + ::/0 with blackhole fill (local.go:6547-6565), LAN prefixes either in LocalRoutes (ExitNodeAllowLANAccess) or pulled into Routes (local.go:6566-6585), service IPs and VIP-service IPs (:6593-6604). wgengine wraps the router in ConsolidatingRoutes on android (userspace.go:348-352) to keep the Builder bundle small. Re-configuration lifecycle: LocalBackend.authReconfig -> wgengine.Reconfig -> CallbackRouter.Set/SetDNS -> ReconfigureVPN -> flush -> (DeepEqual gate) -> app Builder/establish -> new fd -> multiTUN swap. Exit node on/off, subnet route acceptance, MagicDNS/search-domain changes and VIP services therefore re-establish automatically with no app-side heuristics; identical configs never re-establish.
MTU/IPv6: setMtu(1280) (official defaultMTU, tailscale.go:27; multiTUN reports the device's SIOCGIFMTU or 1280). Both families always allowed and both node addresses always added; the old tun_ipv6_enabled toggle would leak IPv6 when ::/0 is routed and is removed.

== 7. What happens to netstack and SOCKS in TUN mode ==
Netstack is still created (cmd/tailscaled/netstack.go:23-42) and wired into the tstun.Wrapper exactly as upstream TUN mode; ProcessLocalIPs=false, ProcessSubnets=true (phone can be exit node/subnet router; netstack forwards inbound traffic to non-local IPs since Android has no kernel forwarding), NetstackRouter=true (hostinfo UserspaceRouter, skips Linux forwarding checks), CheckLocalTransportEndpoints=true. Patches 08/09/11/14 keep governing proxy mode; 09 and 11 are inert under a real TUN; 08 and 14 are active in both. The SOCKS5/HTTP proxies stay on the command line and on loopback/LAN, dialing via netstack for tailnet/exit-node destinations and via the OS (UID-excluded, direct) for everything else, exactly like today's proxy mode. The bridge's DoH client and Taildrive reverse proxy keep using them.

decisions.question: How does the daemon's own control/DERP/WireGuard traffic avoid the TUN?
decisions.recommendation: UID exclusion: keep addDisallowedApplication for every io.github.bropines.tailscaled* package (TunVpnService.kt:230-247). The child shares the UID (daemon.go:51 exec), so every socket bypasses the VPN with zero IPC, no timing window and no DebugRebind hack. Compensate with the hybrid netstack dialer (tailscaled.go:718, netstack.go:42/46, CheckLocalTransportEndpoints) so UserDial reaches the tailnet through netstack.
decisions.alternatives: (B) Faithful port of VpnService.protect(): daemon sends every new socket fd over the channel, app calls protect()+Network.bindSocket, acks; requires the DebugRebind workaround (backend.go:215-244), a synchronous IPC inside every Dialer.Control, fail-open semantics and putting the app inside the VPN (changes where the UI/WebUI/ByeDPI traffic goes). Rejected for a first release; the channel design leaves room to add it later. (C) SO_MARK/policy routing: EPERM without root (netns_android.go:26-28). (D) Talking to /dev/socket/fwmarkd directly from Go: undocumented ABI that changed across releases. Rejected.

decisions.question: How does the fd cross the process boundary, including the 2nd..Nth fd on every re-establish?
decisions.recommendation: An AF_UNIX SOCK_STREAM socketpair created by the bridge, child end inherited via exec.Cmd.ExtraFiles as fd 3 with TS_ANDROID_VPN_FD=3; newline-JSON frames; the TUN fd rides as SCM_RIGHTS on the tun frame (WriteMsgUnix/ReadMsgUnix). The channel is 1:1 with the process generation (fits daemon.go:20-33,113-133), needs no path/permissions/listener, and its EOF doubles as the parent-death signal.
decisions.alternatives: Filesystem unix socket next to tailscaled.sock (needs connect-retry, stale-file handling, permissions; patch 12 territory). ExtraFiles one-shot fd only (cannot re-establish; the first config is not even known at spawn time because LocalAddrs come from the netmap). Kotlin LocalSocket.setFileDescriptorsForSend (second implementation of the same thing; Go already has UnixRights).

decisions.question: Where does the Builder logic live?
decisions.recommendation: Kotlin receives a flat JSON {mtu, addrs, dns, search, routes, excludeRoutes} and only calls Builder methods; the bridge (Go) does all prefix math: masking, loopback skip, excludeRoute only on API 33+, and the pre-33 Routes-minus-LocalRoutes subtraction via a port of libtailscale/ranges_calc (testable with go test).
decisions.alternatives: Official style: Go drives a fine-grained VPNServiceBuilder interface through gomobile (more gomobile surface, more JNI round trips). Daemon computes the final Builder list (needs the SDK level in the daemon and duplicates app knowledge). App derives routes from the IPN bus netmap it already parses (appctr/bus.go) and only pushes fds: duplicates routerConfigLocked/compileConfig and drifts from upstream. Rejected.

decisions.question: Which Router/DNS facade runs inside tailscaled?
decisions.recommendation: Upstream wgengine/router/callback.go CallbackRouter (documented as the Android/iOS/macOS shim) with a store-only SetBoth and the flush in conf.ReconfigureVPN, plus a DeepEqual gate against the last acked pair. Zero copied code for the facade.
decisions.alternatives: Vendor libtailscale/vpnfacade.go (105 lines; functionally identical). router.NewFake + noop DNS with the app deriving everything from the netmap (see above). Letting CallbackRouter.SetBoth flush directly (two round trips and possibly two establishes per Reconfig because Set and SetDNS both call it).

decisions.question: Netstack flags in fd mode
decisions.recommendation: ProcessLocalIPs=false, ProcessSubnets=true, NetstackRouter=true (all as libtailscale/backend.go:352-359) plus CheckLocalTransportEndpoints=true (needed only because of UID exclusion).
decisions.alternatives: NetstackRouter=false as upstream Linux TUN mode (tailscaled.go:881 default): the phone could then not act as exit node/subnet router and hostinfo would differ from the official client. Rejected.

decisions.question: MTU and IPv6
decisions.recommendation: setMtu(1280) fixed (tailscale.go:27, tstun safe MTU); always allowFamily both and add both node addresses; delete tun_ipv6_enabled.
decisions.alternatives: Keep 1500 (TunVpnService.kt:51) or a user setting; keep the IPv6 toggle as a carrier escape hatch (leaks IPv6 when ::/0 is routed, and breaks the fd7a:115c:a1e0::53 resolver). Rejected.

decisions.question: Behaviour when the VPN is revoked (another VPN app) or establish() returns null
decisions.recommendation: Degrade to proxy-only: daemon Down()s and closes the device, keeps running, SOCKS/HTTP proxies keep working; app shows a 'VPN permission lost, tap to re-enable' notification and keeps tun_mode_enabled; next START/APPLY runs TunPermissionActivity and RebuildVpn. Explicit denial in the prepare() dialog still flips tun_mode_enabled off (TunPermissionActivity.kt:51) to avoid prompt loops. Builder errors return ok=false so they land in router health rather than stopping the node.
decisions.alternatives: Official behaviour (IPNService.kt:123-131, backend.go:410-428): WantRunning=false, node stops. Rejected; TailSocks has a useful proxy-only fallback the official app lacks.

decisions.question: Synchronous or asynchronous ReconfigureVPN?
decisions.recommendation: Synchronous with a 20 s ack timeout: wgengine.Reconfig sees Builder failures (INTERACT_ACROSS_USERS, not prepared) as in the official app (backend.go:132-144 configErrs), and a timeout returns an error instead of wedging Reconfig forever; a deferred ack (no VpnService yet) returns nil and the pair is re-sent on want_config.
decisions.alternatives: Fire-and-forget (errors invisible to health; official is synchronous). Block without timeout (a hung app blocks wgengine.Reconfig indefinitely).

decisions.question: multiTUN implementation
decisions.recommendation: Vendor libtailscale/multitun.go verbatim (BSD-3, 394 lines) with defaultMTU=1280.
decisions.alternatives: A ~120-line RWMutex/atomic swap device. Rejected: the blocking semantics (Read pends until a device exists, Down() must unblock Write, tailscale/tailscale#18679) are subtle and the upstream file is battle-tested on exactly this fd-swap workload.

decisions.question: Toggling TUN mode at runtime
decisions.recommendation: A daemon restart via ApplySettings' critical-change list (appctr.go:468-478), because onlyNetstack-dependent state (netns.SetEnabled, ProcessLocalIPs, NetstackRouter, DNS configurator) is fixed in tryEngine. Tasker/AppFunctions/widgets need no change.
decisions.alternatives: Making the engine switchable in-process. Rejected as a large upstream divergence for a rare action.

decisions.question: Settings migration
decisions.recommendation: Keep tun_mode_enabled and tun_excluded_apps; remove tun_address, tun_ipv6_enabled, tun_full_tunnel (dead, MainActivity.kt:410-412) and tun_excluded_cidrs (dead, TunVpnService.kt:180-181); add exit_node_allow_lan mapped to the upstream ExitNodeAllowLANAccess pref through syncSettings; seed it true when a non-default CIDR list existed.
decisions.alternatives: Merge a user CIDR list into LocalRoutes app-side (diverges from upstream, duplicates LAN detection that ipnlocal already does from the interface list once prefix lengths are real).

decisions.question: Parent-death handling
decisions.recommendation: TUN mode: EOF on the control channel makes the daemon exit (no orphan VPN). Proxy mode: unchanged (killLeftoverDaemons at next Start), optionally add TS_PARENT_DEATH_FD later.
decisions.alternatives: TS_PARENT_DEATH_FD pipe for all modes now (would also stop LAN clients' SOCKS when only the app UI process died). Deferred to step 6.

decisions.question: SOCKS5/HTTP proxies and the bridge DNS proxy while the TUN is up
decisions.recommendation: Keep both running: proxies stay on the daemon command line and work via the hybrid dialer; the bridge UDP DNS proxy stays for LAN clients and proxy mode, documented as redundant on-device in TUN mode.
decisions.alternatives: Disable them in TUN mode (breaks LAN-gateway users and the bridge's own DoH/Taildrive consumers).

issues.step: §6 DNS narrative; step 1 (android_vpn.go ctl.baseDNS); step 6 'optional polish'
issues.problem: The DNS section is built on a pref that does not exist. `OverrideDNSResolvers` is not a field anywhere in tailscale v1.102.1, so TailSocks' resolver push in syncSettings is silently discarded by LocalAPI, and the claim 'a DoH resolver makes hasDefaultIPResolversOnly() false so Routes["."] = DefaultResolvers' is false. In this tree DefaultResolvers come only from the netmap (nm.DNS.Resolvers), the exit node's DoH proxy, or FallbackResolvers. For the most common tailnet (MagicDNS on, no global nameservers, no exit node) compileConfig takes the split-DNS branch and calls m.os.GetBaseConfig(); Routes["."] is filled from the *base* nameservers. With a CallbackRouter a nil/failed GetBaseConfigFunc is fatal (only iOS/noopManager may return ErrGetBaseConfigNotSupported), and an empty base config means every non-MagicDNS name SERVFAILs for all VPN-routed apps. So the netstate→baseDNS plumbing is load-bearing for step 1, not step-6 polish, and the 'user removes DoH' reasoning and the 'bridge's DoH client keeps using the proxies' framing (§7) do not describe TUN-mode DNS at all: on-device resolution is plain port-53 forwarding from the daemon's UID-excluded OS sockets to the platform/TS_DNS_FALLBACK resolvers.
issues.evidence: grep -rn OverrideDNS appctr/tailscale_src → only net/dns/nrpt_windows.go:24,352 (Windows NRPT flag); no ipn/prefs.go field. LocalAPI decodes MaskedPrefs with a plain json.Decoder (ipn/localapi/localapi.go:1010-1011) → unknown keys dropped; appctr.go:385-412 builds prefs["OverrideDNSResolvers"]. dnsConfigForNetmap: ipn/ipnlocal/node_backend.go:1510 (CorpDNS gate), 1556-1585 (exit-node DoH / nm.DNS.Resolvers), 1600-1618 (FallbackResolvers only with an exit node). compileConfig: net/dns/manager.go:337-356 (trivial cases), 381-399 (SupportsSplitDNS=false → quad-100), 416-426 (GetBaseConfig; ErrGetBaseConfigNotSupported tolerated only for isIOS || isNoopManager), 447-451 (rcfg.Routes["."] = base.Nameservers). CallbackRouter.GetBaseConfig: wgengine/router/callback.go:75-80. Today it works only via patch 11 + TS_DNS_FALLBACK (appctr/daemon.go:64-68, always non-empty). Official fallback: libtailscale/net.go:283-295 (googleDNSServers when platform DNS is empty).
issues.fix: Rewrite §6/§7: state that DefaultResolvers are netmap/exit-node driven and that GetBaseConfigFunc supplies the '.' upstream. In step 1 make ctl.baseDNS() mandatory and never-empty: LinkProperties dnsServers/domains from netstate frames → TS_DNS_FALLBACK → hard-coded public fallback (mirror net.go:283-295), and set/clear osConfigurationReadWarnable-equivalent health. Remove the dead OverrideDNSResolvers push from syncSettings (or document it as inert) and adjust the DoH setting's UI copy: in TUN mode the DoH URL only affects the bridge's LAN DNS proxy, not on-device resolution. Add an on-device acceptance test: MagicDNS on, no global nameservers, no exit node → `nslookup example.com` from a third-party app succeeds.

issues.step: §2a flush / §2c ctl.run; decision 'Synchronous or asynchronous ReconfigureVPN?'; unspecified error paths
issues.problem: The synchronous flush runs while wgengine holds wgLock, so anything the ctl.run frame loop does must never wait on a wgLock holder or the ack can never arrive (20 s stall, error into Reconfig). The design happens to be safe today (InjectEvent is a non-blocking channel send, dns.Manager.Set releases m.mu before ReconfigureVPN is called, multiTUN.add only talks to its own goroutine) but the invariant is not stated and the frame loop mixes I/O, ioctls and engine calls. Two error paths are also unspecified: (1) the `tun` frame precedes the `ack` — if CreateUnmonitoredTUNFromFD/TUNGETIFF/SIOCGIFINDEX fails in the daemon, or the ack times out and the fd arrives late, the received tun fd must be closed immediately, otherwise the orphaned fd keeps the kernel interface (and the platform's 'VPN connected' state and uid routing) alive with nobody reading it; (2) CallbackRouter.Set mutates the caller's config (NewMTU) and stores the pointer, so the DeepEqual gate must compare the stored pair, not a copy taken before Set.
issues.evidence: wgengine/userspace.go:812-813 (wgLock held for whole Reconfig), 929-931 (reconfigureVPNIfNecessary inside it), 1175-1181 (linkChange also takes wgLock). netmon.go:539-550 (InjectEvent non-blocking). net/dns/manager.go:156-166 (RecompileDNSConfig takes m.mu), 168 (Set). callback.go:45-57 (Set stores rcfg pointer and sets rcfg.NewMTU on first call). multitun.go:153-172 (add path), 233-241 (old device closed, 'hope that no packets are lost'). tun_linux.go:660-689 (CreateUnmonitoredTUNFromFD can fail at SetNonblock/TUNGETIFF).
issues.fix: Document the lock invariant in android_vpn.go; make ctl.run a pure dispatcher (read frame → hand off to per-kind goroutines/channels; ack matching by id) so a slow ioctl or RecompileDNSConfig cannot delay an ack. Specify: on any failure after receiving a tun fd, close it and reply ok=false with the error; on ack timeout, mark the id stale so a late fd is closed on arrival. Shorten the timeout (establish() is sub-second; 5 s is plenty) and log the wait. Compare against the stored pair after Set has run.

issues.problem: The stated reason for switching away from registerDefaultNetworkCallback ('returns the VPN itself once it is up') is wrong for this design: with the app's own UID in addDisallowedApplication the per-app default network is the underlying network, not the VPN (the official comment applies to protect()-based apps whose UID is inside the VPN). The switch to a NOT_VPN NetworkRequest is still a good idea, but it delivers every matching network (Wi-Fi and cellular concurrently), so the design must include a best-network selection equivalent to the official recomputeDefaultNetworkLocked/pickDefaultNetwork or it will feed the wrong iface/gateway/DNS and flip setUnderlyingNetworks. Separately, the current injectIfNeeded enumerates NetworkInterface.getNetworkInterfaces(), which includes tun0 with the node's 100.x/32; if that snapshot ever reaches the daemon's interface getter, HasCGNATInterface becomes true, shouldUseOneCGNATRoute returns false, and every peer change re-establishes the VPN. So SetTailscaleInterfaceProps (per new fd, names change tun0→tun1) is load-bearing, not defensive — and note the official app neither sets it nor filters tun0 from its list, so do not treat upstream Android as proof it is unnecessary.
issues.evidence: TailscaledService.kt:433 (registerDefaultNetworkCallback), 375-400 (getNetworkInterfaces snapshot incl. tun0); TunVpnService.kt:230-247 (own-UID exclusion). Official: NetworkChangeCallback.kt:77-93 (NOT_VPN request, comment about protect()), 171-186 (recomputeDefaultNetworkLocked), App.kt:343-376 (getInterfacesAsJson includes all interfaces, no tun filter); libtailscale has no SetTailscaleInterfaceProps call. Daemon: net/netmon/state.go:562-580 (isTailscaleInterface: registered name or 'tailscale*' only), 893-908 (HasCGNATInterface), interfaces.go:58-64 (index 0 → net.Interfaces(), silently unset on failure); ipn/ipnlocal/local.go:6117 (version.OS()=runtime.GOOS, so the hostinfo masquerade in patch 06 does not affect it), 6216-6226.
issues.fix: Correct the rationale; port pickDefaultNetwork (prefer validated, non-metered/Wi-Fi, else cellular) and only forward that network's LinkProperties in netstate frames plus its Network to setUnderlyingNetworks. Ensure the daemon-side getter never sees tun*/VPN interfaces (filter by NOT_VPN capability, and defensively drop names matching the registered TS interface). Keep SetTailscaleInterfaceProps per fd and add a log assertion in the device test: exactly one 100.64.0.0/10 route across several netmap deliveries.

issues.problem: Closing the control channel in releaseGoResources makes the daemon exit(1) on every *deliberate* Stop/ApplySettings restart, before the bridge has killed it. The supervisor goroutine then sees a non-nil error, logs 'tailscaled cmd crashed' and, if the generation is still current, calls Stop() and CloseCallBack.Close() (stopMe) — turning an intended stop or TunMode toggle into a crash report and a possible extra service shutdown. Root Mode is unaffected (no channel), proxy mode too, but the new path needs an explicit ordering.
issues.evidence: appctr.go:559-585 (supervisor: err → 'tailscaled cmd crashed', isCurrentGeneration, Stop(), CloseCallBack.Close()); appctr.go:758-795 (releaseGoResources runs before/independently of process kill); daemon.go:20-33, 113-133 (generation logic covers only launch supersession); design §2c 'EOF/error on the channel … os.Exit(1)'.
issues.fix: Order the stop path as: bump generation → signal/kill daemon → wait → then close the channel; have the daemon exit with a distinct code (e.g. 0 after a clean 'down' frame, non-zero only on unexpected EOF) and make the supervisor treat the EOF-exit as expected when the generation was retired. Test: TunMode toggle and a plain Stop produce no 'crashed' log and no double stopMe().

issues.step: §6 DNS when AcceptDNS (CorpDNS) is off; Builder input
issues.problem: With CorpDNS=false dnsConfigForNetmap returns before adding any resolvers/routes, compileConfig hits the trivial case and the OSConfig has no nameservers, so the Builder is established with zero DNS servers. The design does not say what the VpnService should do then (Android falls back to the underlying network's DNS in most cases, but ChromeOS erases DNS — the official app injects Google DNS for that reason), and the daemon's quad-100 will still be reachable but unused. Also, if the tailnet sets only IP global nameservers and MagicDNS is off, the Builder legitimately receives those IPs and no quad-100 — the UI banner/health text must not assume quad-100.
issues.evidence: ipn/ipnlocal/node_backend.go:1510 (return when !CorpDNS); net/dns/manager.go:332-336 (needsOSResolver false → empty OSConfig), 337-351 (IP-only resolvers handed straight to the OS); official libtailscale/net.go:69-77, 111-115 (avoidEmptyDNS → googleDNSServers).
issues.fix: Define: when dcfg has no nameservers, either add the current underlying network's DNS servers to the Builder (from the same LinkProperties used for netstate) or document reliance on platform fallback and add the ChromeOS/empty-DNS guard. Cover 'AcceptDNS off' and 'IP-only global nameservers' in the step-3 acceptance list.
